newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Feb 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Feb 12.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Wednesday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:

* Time Warner reported a nearly 80 percent rise in fourth-quarter earnings, beating analysts estimates, and said it had an understanding with partner U S West that would let it cut some of its cable holdings and its debt.
* The dollar rose again, despite comments from the G-7 and U.S. Treasury Secretery Robert Rubin indicating that the currency had risen enough.
* Russian steelmakers are affecting the crowded U.S. market, spurring trade complaints and worries that prices could fall even further.
* Productivity rose 2.2 percent in the fourth quarter, the fastest quarterly rate in three years.
* Officials on both sides of the contract talks with American Airlines pilots say neither the airline nor its pilots have made new offers after two days of negotiations.
* New types of regional jets and who will fly them could prove a key issue in the talks between American Airlines and its pilots.
* Centennial Technologies fired its chairman and chief executive, Emanuel Pinez, removed its chief financial officer and said it is examining its previous financial results.
* China told U.S. officials that it will make some major changes in opening its doors to foreign competition in the negotiations over its entry to the World Trade Organization.
* Ameritech withdrew its request to offer long-distance service after federal regulators reprimanded it for inaccuracies in its filing.
* In an effort to lower overall claims costs, at least three big insurers have started using letters or personal visits to contact crash victims before they hire attorneys.
* Baesa, PepsiCo's Latin American bottler, reported a quarterly loss of $16.7 million.
* Applied Materials reported an 83 percent drop in its fiscal first-quarter net, but its profit before charges was better than expected.
* WHX President James Wareham said he would resign March 1 and also resign as chief executive of the company's Wheeling-Pittsburgh unit.
* Oakwood Counselors and its president agreed to pay more than $450,000 in the Security and Exchange Commission's inquiry into alleged "soft dollar" abuses in the financial industry.
* Can a convicted felon who runs a subprime auto lender raise $100 million in today's market? You betcha.

Ugly Duckling, which is in the business of financing its own sales of used cars to individuals with troubled credit or employment histories, sold five million new shares Monday at $18.625 each. -- Heard on the Street.

* Bonds were largely unchanged in the second straight day of lackluster trading, as wary investors assessed the market's ability to absorb the planned sale of almost $40 billion of new Treasury bonds this week. -- Credit Markets.
